It is one of the largest and most liquid financial markets globally.\",\"At its core, Forex trading involves speculating on the relative value of different currencies. Traders aim to profit from fluctuations in exchange rates between currency pairs, such as EUR/USD or GBP/JPY. The Forex market operates 24 hours a day, five days a week, allowing traders to engage in trading activities at any time.\",\"Forex trading is also sometimes used loosely to refer to CFD (Contract for Difference) trading. CFDs are instruments that allow traders to speculate on the price movements of various assets—such as shares, indices, commodities, cryptocurrencies, and fiat currencies—without owning the underlying asset.\",\"Forex trading has several advantages, such as high liquidity, low transaction costs, and access to leverage. Leverage enables traders to control larger positions with a smaller amount of capital. However, leverage also increases the risk of losses, so traders should always assess their risk tolerance and develop appropriate trading strategies before entering the market.\",\"Whether Forex trading is profitable for an individual trader depends on their ability to analyze the market, implement a sound trading strategy, and manage risks effectively.\",\"Success in Forex trading requires continuous learning, adaptability, and discipline. Requesting technical support may require accessing other data related to the notifying user, depending on the nature of the incident.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003eSending commercial information and promotions:\u003c/strong\u003e User data may be used to notify new functions incorporated into the system, as well as commercial information about the services offered by FXStreet, including, among others, discounts and other offers.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003eSecurity audits:\u003c/strong\u003e Data on the use of FXStreet services may be internally analyzed to detect potential fraud and violations of the service's Terms and Conditions, as well as to carry out treatments required by law.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003eStatistics:\u003c/strong\u003e Usage profiles may be analyzed by FXStreet to study behavior and preferences, with the aim of improving the user experience and its services.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003eIntegration with third-party services:\u003c/strong\u003e FXStreet may process data from its users to provide access to applications integrated with the service, such as automated and/or direct sending of data incorporated into the platform to third-party applications.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003eOther purposes:\u003c/strong\u003e FXStreet's use of the user's personal data for purposes other than those indicated in this privacy policy will require informing the user and, if applicable, obtaining their consent.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003eSelection:\u003c/strong\u003e Evaluate and manage, where appropriate, your Curriculum Vitae for selection processes that fit your professional profile and carry out the necessary actions for the selection and hiring of personnel.\",\"Likewise, said data will be processed for subsequent anonymization and grouping for the purpose of statistically analyzing trends and profiling groups to improve the services offered by FXStreet.\",\"All fields in the forms must be completed for FXStreet to fulfill the purposes mentioned above. In the case of optional fields in a form, they will be expressly indicated.\",\"The user may object to the sending of commercial communications at any time by sending an email to the address indicated above, or through the corresponding section in the user profile of the platform offered by FXStreet.\",\"In addition to specific treatments according to the service you request, FXStreet may store the IP address of users' devices, only for technical and security reasons, and therefore, based on the legitimate interest of safeguarding the integrity and security of the service.\"]},{\"title\":\"5. LEGAL BASIS FOR DATA PROCESSING\",\"paragraphs\":[\"The processing of personal data provided by the user is based on the following legal bases that legitimize it:\",\"Through the completion of forms on the Web, participation in selection procedures, or by sending emails or any other type of information request sent to FXStreet, the interested party provides their express consent for the processing of their personal data. Likewise, with regard to the provision of the service indicated in the previous section, FXStreet will process your personal data for the execution of the subscription contract for the service.\",\"Likewise, your data may be used based on the legitimate interest in promoting our services and disseminating our brand through marketing actions, provided that such interest does not prevail over fundamental rights and freedoms that require the protection of personal data.\",\"When a user joins Telegram groups managed by FXStreet, the interested party provides their express consent for the processing of their personal data, including their use for marketing activities, in this case, limited to receiving publications made in the channel they have joined, without being used individually for personalization of the received advertising, or the use of private messages to send such content, without prejudice to the identification of promoted third-party services.\",\"This consent will be understood as free, specific, informed, and unequivocal since, after reading this Privacy Policy, the user is informed and, if they agree, can accept it through a declaration or a clear affirmative action, such as marking a checkbox provided for this purpose or joining groups in instant messaging applications from the client installed on their chosen device.\",\"In no case will FXStreet use the personal data of interested parties for purposes other than those mentioned above, and undertakes to keep due professional secrecy and to establish the necessary technical and organizational measures to safeguard the information provided by its users.\"]},{\"title\":\"6. APPLICABLE PRINCIPLES FOR DATA PROCESSING\",\"paragraphs\":[\"In the processing of the personal data of its users, FXStreet will apply the following principles that comply with the requirements of the new European data protection regulation:\",\"\u003cstrong\u003ePrinciple of lawfulness, fairness, and transparency:\u003c/strong\u003e Your consent will always be required for the processing of personal data, specifying one or more purposes that will be previously informed with absolute transparency.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003ePrinciple of data minimization:\u003c/strong\u003e Only the strictly necessary data for the purposes required will be requested. Likewise, in the case of optional additional data that may allow for greater personalization of the service, their optional nature will be expressly indicated.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003ePrinciple of limitation of storage period:\u003c/strong\u003e Data will be stored for no longer than necessary for the purposes of the processing.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003ePrinciple of integrity and confidentiality:\u003c/strong\u003e Your data will be processed in a way that ensures adequate security and guarantees confidentiality.\"]},{\"title\":\"7. DATA COMMUNICATION\",\"paragraphs\":[\"In general, FXStreet will not communicate this personal data to third parties, except when providing a service requires a contractual relationship with a data processor and it is strictly necessary to manage and maintain the relationship between the user and said company, such as financial entities through which payment management is carried out. This will only be done for the time necessary to enable the execution of the processing contract, and under the same conditions and with the same responsibilities required of the controller.\",\"On the other hand, third parties who have a legal or contractual obligation with FXStreet to provide access to this personal data will have the right to access it, including, for example, the Ombudsman and Judges and Courts interested in related proceedings with submitted claims, as well as other competent Public Administrations, in cases provided by law and for the purposes defined therein.\"]},{\"title\":\"8. RIGHTS OF THE INTERESTED PARTIES\",\"paragraphs\":[\"The user may exercise at any time, under the terms established by current legislation, the rights to access, rectify or deletion of data, request the restriction of processing of their personal data, object to it, request the portability of their data, as well as revoke the consent given, rights recognized in the aforementioned Regulation (EU). The user may exercise these rights by contacting FXStreet at the address of its registered office indicated above; by sending an email to the following address privacy@fxstreet.com or to the postal address c/Portaferrisa 7 08002 Barcelona, Spain.\",\"Interested parties may access their personal data, obtain confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning them is being processed, as well as request the rectification of inaccurate data or, where appropriate, request its deletion when, among other reasons, the data is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was collected. Under certain circumstances, interested parties may request the restriction of the processing of their data, in which case it will only be kept for the exercise or defense of claims that may arise.\",\"Interested parties may also object to the processing of their data. In this case, FXStreet will stop processing the data, except for compelling legitimate reasons, or the exercise or defense of possible claims.\",\"As an interested party, you have the right to receive the personal data that concerns you, in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format, and to transmit them to another data controller when:\",\"The processing is based on consent.\",\"The data has been provided by the interested party.\",\"The processing is carried out by automated means.\",\"When exercising your right to data portability, you will have the right to have personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another, where technically feasible.\",\"Regarding treatments based on user consent, you can withdraw such consent at any time. However, withdrawing your consent will not affect the lawfulness of the processing carried out under your consent before its withdrawal, and will not affect the lawfulness of the processing we continue to carry out under any other legal basis.\",\"For the effective exercise of these rights, the user must prove their identity by providing their name and surname, a photocopy of their ID or equivalent identifying document that proves their identity, a request that specifies the request, an address for notifications, and the date and signature of the requester.\",\"Likewise, the user may file a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (the competent supervisory authority in this matter), especially when they have not obtained satisfaction in the exercise of their rights, by sending a letter to the following address: C/Jorge Juan, nº 6, 28001 - Madrid, or through the website: https://www.agpd.es\"]},{\"title\":\"9. RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN\",\"paragraphs\":[\"By using this website, you acknowledge and agree that you have the right to request that your personal data be erased or forgotten in accordance with applicable data protection laws. If you wish to exercise this right, please contact us using the contact information provided on our website.\",\"We will consider all requests for erasure or forgotten data in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. In some cases, we may be required to retain certain data for legal or regulatory reasons. If we are unable to comply with your request for erasure or forgotten data, we will inform you of the reasons for our inability to do so.\",\"Please note that the right to be forgotten is not an absolute right, and may be limited in certain circumstances. For example, we may be required to retain certain data for legal or regulatory reasons, or to exercise or defend legal claims. Additionally, erasure or forgotten data may not be possible if it is necessary for the performance of a contract or service that you have requested.\",\"We will make reasonable efforts to ensure that any personal data that is retained is accurate and up-to-date. You have the right to request that any inaccurate data be corrected or updated.\",\"We may update these terms and conditions from time to time. Any changes will be posted on our website, and your continued use of our website will be deemed acceptance of any updated terms and conditions.\",\"By using our website, you agree to the terms and conditions set out in this section on the right to be forgotten.\"]},{\"title\":\"10. DATA BREACHES\",\"paragraphs\":[\"We take the security of your personal information very seriously and have implemented measures to protect against unauthorized access, alteration, or disclosure. In the event of a data breach, we will take appropriate steps to notify affected users and authorities as required by law.\",\"If we become aware of a data breach that compromises the security of your personal information, we will take steps to investigate the breach and mitigate any harm. This may include notifying affected users, updating our security measures, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies.\",\"We are not responsible for any harm or damages resulting from a data breach that is beyond our control, including but not limited to attacks by malicious third parties or natural disasters. However, we will take all reasonable measures to prevent and mitigate any potential breaches.\",\"By using our services, you acknowledge that no method of transmission over the internet or electronic storage is 100% secure, and you agree to assume any risk associated with the security of your personal information.\"]},{\"title\":\"11. In such cases, we will ensure that the transfer is lawful and that appropriate safeguards are in place to protect your personal data, such as standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission, binding corporate rules, or other adequate measures.\",\"Certain data may be transferred to the US. First, by highlighting services tailored to the traders' interests, we uncover new solutions for their needs. Second, by funding FXStreet's mission, we can keep helping traders in their journey.\",\"Advertising is the best model to ensure our services remain open and free to every trader in the world, but at the same time, it can generate incentives that are not aligned with our users. For that, and because keeping traders' trust is critical for FXStreet, we are forthcoming in explaining how we collaborate with our advertisers. This transparency allows our audience to make fully informed decisions.\",\"FXStreet offers various advertising models to partners, including display ads, sponsorships, broker listings, and custom solutions, including branded and sponsored content. These products allow brokerages and financial firms to reach FXStreet's large audience of traders.\",\"The company clearly differentiates between independent content and branded materials.\"],\"sections\":[{\"title\":\"Maintaining editorial independence\",\"paragraphs\":[\"Every day, FXStreet's editorial team works hard to guarantee the best market coverage and help traders make informed decisions, generating dozens of articles covering all sessions and multiple markets.\",\"We are committed to the highest standards of editorial integrity. FXStreet's editorial content is produced independently by our team of market analysts, reporters and editors. In each article, you will find the author(s) of the content at the top. We guarantee that our in-house written news and analysis are free from any commercial interests.\"]},{\"title\":\"Branded content and sponsored placements\",\"paragraphs\":[\"On the other hand, FXStreet always prominently tag branded content as BRANDED or SPONSORED to identify that these articles and pages have been paid for by an advertiser, and differentiate them from editorial content.\",\"While we strive to be comprehensive, the compensation we receive for publishing this type of content can influence the products, companies, or services we showcase and review. Compensation can be in the form of fixed fees – in exchange for exposure –, or variable fees – in exchange for metrics such as clicks or registrations.\",\"By transparently disclosing this information, FXStreet ensures that its users understand the nature of the content they are consuming and can take that into account to make informed decisions about the products and services they choose to engage with.\"]},{\"title\":\"A win-win-win model\",\"paragraphs\":[\"FXStreet's advertising partnerships are crucial to its business model, allowing it to provide free, high-quality content. By balancing editorial independence and advertising needs, FXStreet maintains the trust and integrity of its platform, and aligns the interests of the company, its users and its advertisers.\"]}],\"closing\":\"Feel free to share your doubts and we will be happy to address them. You can contact us at \u003cemail\u003econtact@fxstreet.com\u003c/email\u003e.\",\"contactEmail\":\"contact@fxstreet.com\",\"seo\":{\"title\":\"FXStreet's Advertising Model - FXStreet\",\"description\":\"Learn how FXStreet's advertising model funds free, high-quality content while maintaining editorial independence. Discover our transparency about branded content and sponsored placements.\"}},\"how-we-score-reviews\":{\"title\":\"How does FXStreet review and score brokers?\",\"intro\":[\"\u003cstrong\u003eAt FXStreet, we strive to offer an honest and impartial assessment of brokers you may be considering.\u003c/strong\u003e Our reviews combine in-depth research with hands-on testing, reflecting the real-world experience of opening and using a brokerage account.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003eWe understand that every trader has different needs,\u003c/strong\u003e so rather than assign a single overall score, we break down our reviews across six categories.\u003cbr/\u003eEach of these is scored individually based on how well the broker performs in relevant subcategories.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003eWhile brokers do pay to be reviewed, our analysts and writers work with full editorial independence.\u003c/strong\u003e FXStreet has always taken the trader's side, and principles of accuracy, transparency, and objectivity guide our content. Our goal is to save you time and potential frustration by helping you find a broker that aligns with your needs before you commit your funds.\"],\"sections\":[{\"title\":\"Account Conditions\",\"paragraphs\":[\"We assess the cost, flexibility, and ease of setting up and funding an account. The less friction involved, the higher the score. Key criteria include:\"],\"criteria\":[{\"title\":\"Account Types \u0026 Minimum Deposit\",\"content\":\"Brokers offering multiple account types, including Islamic and demo accounts, with low or no minimum deposits score higher. Limited account types or high deposit requirements reduce the score.\"},{\"title\":\"Costs \u0026 Fees\",\"content\":\"Transparent brokers with low spreads, commissions, and swap rates, as well as minimal non-trading fees (inactivity, deposit, withdrawal) earn top marks. Higher or hidden costs lower the rating.\"},{\"title\":\"Bonuses \u0026 Promotions\",\"content\":\"Points are awarded for accessible welcome offers, loyalty schemes, and achievable referral programs. A lack of promotions or unachievable terms will reduce scores.\"},{\"title\":\"Depositing \u0026 Withdrawing Ease\",\"content\":\"Brokers that offer fast, diverse, low-cost funding and withdrawal methods in multiple currencies rate higher. Delays, restrictions, high fees, or limited options result in a lower score.\"}],\"closing\":\"Points are allocated depending on the breadth, speed, accessibility, and affordability of the broker's offering.\"},{\"title\":\"Trading Settings\",\"paragraphs\":[\"We review the broker's trading environment, flexibility, and execution performance:\"],\"criteria\":[{\"title\":\"Asset \u0026 Instrument Variety\",\"content\":\"A broader range of tradable markets (e.g., FX, indices, commodities, crypto, CFDs, futures, ETFs) and instruments available within them earn more points. A limited offering will reduce the score.\"},{\"title\":\"Leverage\",\"content\":\"High but responsibly managed leverage, adjusted for regulatory regions, is rewarded. Minimal or no leverage options score lower.\"},{\"title\":\"Execution Quality\",\"content\":\"We perform \u003cstrong\u003ereal account testing\u003c/strong\u003e across multiple asset classes to evaluate how a broker handles trade execution in real conditions. This includes a detailed assessment of \u003cstrong\u003etransparency, order types, execution speed, and performance.\u003c/strong\u003e\",\"followUp\":[\"We test for \u003cstrong\u003eslippage, order rejections, and spread consistency.\u003c/strong\u003e Brokers using transparent ECN or DMA models with a wide range of advanced order types, such as trailing stops or bracket orders, are rated more favorably.\",\"We also examine whether trades are filled promptly and at the expected prices, particularly during \u003cstrong\u003ehigh-volume sessions.\u003c/strong\u003e Those that experience delays, \u003cstrong\u003epoor fill accuracy, frequent requotes, or widening spreads\u003c/strong\u003e during stable market conditions will see their scores impacted accordingly.\",\"This scoring is entirely experimental and based on actual trading experience.\"]},{\"title\":\"Trading Conditions\",\"content\":\"Brokers that allow hedging, scalping, and algorithmic trading earn additional points. Restrictions on these features may result in a lower score.\"}],\"closing\":\"Scores are determined based on range, flexibility, and real-time test performance.\"},{\"title\":\"Tools \u0026 Resources\",\"paragraphs\":[\"We assess how well a broker supports a trader's journey with platforms, tools, and education:\"],\"criteria\":[{\"title\":\"Trading Platforms\",\"content\":\"MT4/5, cTrader, TradingView, and in-house platforms are scored on customization, speed, and usability. Outdated or clunky platforms with limited features receive lower scores.\"},{\"title\":\"Copy Trading \u0026 PAMM/MAM\",\"content\":\"Tools that support copy trading and capital management, such as PAMM or MAM accounts, are evaluated based on their integration and management capabilities. Brokers offering proprietary or in-house solutions receive higher scores due to \u003cstrong\u003egreater oversight and control\u003c/strong\u003e of performance and risk.\",\"followUp\":[\"Third-party integrations, while still valuable, typically score lower because the broker has limited influence over the quality of fund management. Limited, outdated, or low-quality content lowers the score.\"},{\"title\":\"Trader Tools\",\"content\":\"Brokers offering calendars, sentiment indicators, calculators, VPS, and news feeds receive the highest scores. Missing tools or limited functionality result in reduced points.\"}],\"closing\":\"Points are assigned based on variety, usefulness, and quality of available tools and content.\"},{\"title\":\"Trust\",\"paragraphs\":[\"This is our most heavily weighted category. Approval from only one major regulator can still be viewed positively, while regulation from emerging market jurisdictions earns moderate recognition. Brokers with minimal or no regulatory oversight receive lower trust scores\"]},{\"title\":\"Regulatory Alerts\",\"content\":\"Brokers with no warnings or unresolved issues score higher. Multiple or major unresolved alerts significantly lower scores.\"},{\"title\":\"Client Protections\",\"content\":\"Negative balance protection, segregated funds, and compensation schemes all add points. The absence of these protections results in a lower score.\"},{\"title\":\"Reputation\",\"content\":[\"This score reflects FXStreet's editorial opinion, alongside aggregated feedback from respected platforms such as ForexPeaceArmy, Trustpilot, and others. We consider the overall sentiment of user reviews, any unresolved regulatory complaints, and our own experience from the hands-on testing process.\",\"\u003cstrong\u003eConsistent positive feedback and transparency are rewarded\u003c/strong\u003e, while poor user experiences or unresolved issues result in a reduced score.\"]},{\"title\":\"Stability\",\"content\":\"We assess a broker's long-term operational track record and consistency. Brokers with many years in business and a stable brand identity tend to inspire greater trust. A long history of uninterrupted operations and minimal name changes is viewed positively, as it signals \u003cstrong\u003ereliability and resilience\u003c/strong\u003e. Those with multiple name changes in a short period score lower.\"}],\"closing\":\"Points are allocated based on transparency, credibility, and investor safety.\"},{\"title\":\"Customer Support\",\"paragraphs\":[\"We evaluate the quality, reach, and responsiveness of the broker's support team:\"],\"criteria\":[{\"title\":\"Languages\",\"content\":\"Brokers offering multilingual support score higher. Brokers with limited or outdated communication options score lower.\"},{\"title\":\"Support Schedule\",\"content\":\"Brokers offering 24/7 customer support are rated highest. Reduced scores are given when support is limited to business hours or doesn't align with major global trading sessions.\"},{\"title\":\"Response Times\",\"content\":\"We submit real queries and time the responses. Here is how we analyze every aspect a trader might consider when selecting a broker.\"}},\"how-fxstreet-uses-ai\":{\"title\":\"How FXStreet uses AI\",\"intro\":[\"At FXStreet, \u003cstrong\u003etransparency\u003c/strong\u003e is one of our editorial values. We have always aimed to earn our audience's trust by being open about what we do, why we do it, and how we do it. As Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) becomes more widely used in newsrooms around the world, we believe it is our responsibility to \u003cstrong\u003eexplain how we use AI\u003c/strong\u003e in our day-to-day editorial operations.\",\"While AI is helping us improve some workflows and tools, \u003cstrong\u003eFXStreet remains fully committed to human-led content\u003c/strong\u003e. Our editorial team strives to provide top-notch, timely, and insightful market coverage every day, written and reviewed by our experienced analysts for traders. AI supports our work, but \u003cstrong\u003eit does not replace the editorial judgment, market expertise, and accountability of FXStreet's team\u003c/strong\u003e.\",\"AI use at FXStreet is governed by a \u003cstrong\u003estrict editorial policy\u003c/strong\u003e. Our internal guidelines recognize AI as a useful tool for both reporting, writing, and workflow support, but only under \u003cstrong\u003estrict human supervision and clearly defined limits.\u003c/strong\u003e\"],\"sectionsHeading\":\"So, how are we using AI?\",\"sections\":[{\"title\":\"Create in-house tools\",\"paragraphs\":[\"We use AI to enhance market intelligence through tools built in line with our editorial standards. One example is the FXStreet Speech Tracker, which parses and scores the tone of central bank speeches in real-time. This helps traders quickly assess whether policymakers are hawkish or dovish without having to read full statements, giving instant insight.\"]},{\"title\":\"Improving efficiency\",\"paragraphs\":[\"We also use AI to help the newsroom spend less time on certain tasks, such as tagging articles or drafting headline suggestions. Other AI tools help simplify parts of the technical analysis workflow or summarize external content, including material provided by banks, brokerages, and external analysts. These tools have taken months to develop, are designed to align with our editorial standards, and remain under constant review.\"]},{\"title\":\"Translations\",\"paragraphs\":[\"To translate content originally written in English to other languages, we use a self-training AI translation system that draws on an extensive glossary of specific terms related to financial markets and economics. Most of the content is verified by editors: when that's the case, the reader sees the \\\"verified translation\\\" label, while those labeled with the \\\"machine translation\\\" tag have not.\"]},{\"title\":\"Images\",\"paragraphs\":[\"Images displayed on FXStreet's platforms have mostly been created using AI tools. This process is subject to strict guardrails. Images portraying public figures must be easily distinguishable from real photographs, should strive for neutrality, and must respect copyright rules, among other conditions.\"]},{\"title\":\"Being transparent and accountable\",\"paragraphs\":[\"Almost all AI-assisted editorial content is reviewed by an editor before publication. When AI has assisted in the creation of an article, a disclaimer will be included at the end of the piece. Internally, each writer and editor remains accountable for any mistakes or inaccuracies related to the use of AI.\"]}],\"closing\":\"Using AI to write articles from scratch or to rewrite them is forbidden, as is using AI tools that haven't been trained and validated by the editorial team. When decision-makers at the Fed signal the path of interest is lower, their speech is dovish. Indications of higher interest rates are hawkish.\",\"linkPath\":\"/macroeconomics/central-banks/fed\",\"faq\":{\"whyNoScoreTitle\":\"Why is there no Sentiment/Score in this speech?\",\"whyNoScoreDescription\":\"Sometimes, central bankers are scheduled to make public appearances but they do not talk about monetary policy, failing to make any impact on markets. When this happens, the result of the speech in our Economic Calendar will be N/A.\",\"fedSpeakersTitle\":\"Who are the Fed speakers?\",\"fedSpeakersDescription\":\"Markets are always adjusting to the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) future interest rate projections. There are 17 FOMC board members, but only 12 of them actually vote on the FOMC meetings, held eight times a year.\",\"howWorksTitle\":\"How does it work?\",\"howWorksDescription\":\"We have developed a custom AI model that analyzes all the relevant speeches by the FOMC members and rates them on a dove-hawk scale. This allows us to provide traders with real-time notifications on how each word of Fedspeak impacts the US Dollar.\"}}},\"commodities\":{\"pageTitle\":\"Commodities Market\",\"seo\":{\"title\":\"Commodities FX Related\",\"description\":\"Follow the S\u0026P WCI, the USD index and commodity currencies with charts, news and analysis.\"},\"editorialText\":{\"left\":[{\"title\":\"Commodities Explained\",\"paragraphs\":[{\"text\":\"\u003cstrong\u003eCommodities are raw materials or basic products used to produce other goods or deliver services. They often take center stage during inflationary periods,\u003c/strong\u003e serving as a hedge against inflation. \u003clink\u003eGold\u003c/link\u003e, in particular, has an important psychological value \u003cstrong\u003eas a hedge against economic uncertainty.\u003c/strong\u003e\",\"linkPath\":\"https://www.fxstreet.com/markets/commodities/metals/gold\"},\"But other commodities can also signal shifts in economic cycles. A bottom and rise in copper prices - widely regarded as a barometer of economic health - may signal bearish conditions for bonds and utilities, which are sensitive to interest rate changes.\",{\"text\":\"Energy prices impact the whole economy, besides having a psychological effect on inflation. Rising oil prices, for instance, act as a \\\"tax\\\" on the economy as it tends to slow growth prospects. This often turns into lower interest rates and higher \u003clink\u003ebond prices\u003c/link\u003e.\",\"linkPath\":\"https://www.fxstreet.com/bonds\"}]},{\"title\":\"Commodities and the US Dollar\",\"paragraphs\":[\"Commodities, priced in US dollars, tend to have an inverse relationship with the USD. A strong USD often puts downward pressure on commodity prices, making them less attractive to investors.\"]},{\"title\":\"Commodity groups\",\"paragraphs\":[\"Similar to industry sectors in equity markets, the commodity market consists of several groups, each providing different economic signals.\",{\"text\":\"Some commodities, specifically the metals group, are considered \u003cstrong\u003etangible assets\u003c/strong\u003e because they are non-perishable. Meanwhile, Silver and Gold have the advantage of consistent specifications across nations, unlike \u003clink\u003eTexas\u003c/link\u003e and Brent crude Oil, which differ in composition.\",\"linkPath\":\"https://www.fxstreet.com/rates-charts/westtexasintermediate\"}],\"bullets\":[{\"text\":\"\u003cstrong\u003ePrecious metals:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003clink\u003eGold\u003c/link\u003e, Silver, Platinum, and Palladium. Copper, despite being used primarily for industrial purposes, is usually also lumped into this category. Precious metals are very popular among Forex traders due to their perceived monetary value.\",\"linkPath\":\"https://www.fxstreet.com/markets/commodities/metals/gold\"},{\"text\":\"\u003cstrong\u003eEnergy:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003clink\u003eOil\u003c/link\u003e is the most prone to supply shocks, political tensions in Oil-producing countries or regions, policies from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), and volatile demand from emerging countries. These factors create significant risks for those trading in this market. Higher Oil prices tend to negatively impact equities, raising the prospects of higher inflation and slower growth.\",\"linkPath\":\"https://www.fxstreet.com/markets/commodities/energy/oil\"},{\"text\":\"\u003cstrong\u003eGrains:\u003c/strong\u003e Grain prices fluctuate on the so-called crop year, with planting and harvesting forming tradable price cycles. However, those cycles are influenced by unpredictable weather conditions. Key \u003cstrong\u003eagricultural\u003c/strong\u003e commodities include Corn, Soybeans, Wheat and Oats.\"},{\"text\":\"\u003cstrong\u003eSoft commodities:\u003c/strong\u003e This category includes coffee, orange juice, cocoa, sugar and cotton.\"}]}],\"right\":[{\"title\":\"Commodity Currencies\",\"paragraphs\":[\"\u003cstrong\u003eCommodity currencies\u003c/strong\u003e are said to be correlated with the price of commodities. The Australian dollar, the Canadian dollar and the New Zealand dollar are considered commodity currencies because the economies backed by the named currencies are \u003cstrong\u003esensitive to commodity valuations\u003c/strong\u003e. In this light, be sure to factor in the global economic outlook when evaluating any of the commodity currencies. In any case, correlation is not causation and such relationships can and do break down.\"]},{\"title\":\"AUD\",\"paragraphs\":[\"Being China a tremendous consumer of raw materials, and Australia \u003cstrong\u003ea leading exporter of metals, coal and grains\u003c/strong\u003e, market perceptions of strong demand from China could see the Australian dollar gain in sympathy with commodity prices. The boom in Asian regional growth over the past decade has supported the Australian economy, bringing with it higher levels of inflation. This explains why the RBA maintained higher interest rates than other major central banks.\",{\"text\":\"Visit \u003clink\u003ea dedicated AUD/USD page\u003c/link\u003e.\",\"linkPath\":\"https://www.fxstreet.com/currencies/audusd\"}]},{\"title\":\"CAD\",\"paragraphs\":[\"Canada \u003cstrong\u003eis the fifth largest gold producer and fourteenth largest oil producer\u003c/strong\u003e. Thereby, strong commodity prices generally benefit domestic producers and increase their income from exports. There is a caveat, though, and that is the positive correlation makes the Canadian dollar more expensive in USD terms. Since Canada's economy is very dependent on external demand from the United States, a strong CAD could filter into reduced demand for Canadian Exports.\",{\"text\":\"Visit \u003clink\u003ea dedicated USD/CAD page\u003c/link\u003e.\",\"linkPath\":\"https://www.fxstreet.com/currencies/usdcad\"}]},{\"title\":\"NZD\",\"paragraphs\":[{\"text\":\"New Zealand \u003cstrong\u003eis primarily an agricultural-commodity-producing economy\u003c/strong\u003e (dairy products and meat in particular), and therefore it displays a weaker correlation than CAD and AUD to metal and energy prices. But still, it is highly sensitive to global performance, especially of its key trading partners, Australia, United States and Japan. It's commodity currency status is also to be understood via its dependency on the Australian economy, and since Australia is very commodity driven, any changes affecting the Australian economy affect New Zealand as well. Against the Japanese yen, the NZD can bee regarded as a \u003clink\u003erisk barometer\u003c/link\u003e.\",\"linkPath\":\"https://www.fxstreet.com/technical-analysis/sentiment/risk-appetite\"}]},{\"title\":\"How bullish are commodity currencies and the USD against a basket of 21 world currencies?\",\"paragraphs\":[{\"text\":\"The \u003cstrong\u003eBullish Percentage Index\u003c/strong\u003e compares the four majors against the 21 most traded currencies (according to the \u003clink\u003eBIS statistics\u003c/link\u003e). Among these currencies are the Korean Won, the Mexican Peso, the Turkish Lira, the Brazilian Real, etc. It shows the percentage of currency crosses on buy signals on Point and Figure charts. Point and Figure charts have the particularity of being objectively bullish or bearish, depending on the most recent double-top/bottom buy or sell signal. The Bullish Percentage Index is \u003cstrong\u003ea breadth indicator\u003c/strong\u003e used in stock indices, and its logic has been adopted by FXStreet.com to measure currency strength.\",\"linkPath\":\"https://www.bis.org/\"},\"The index can be read as an \u003cstrong\u003eoscillator\u003c/strong\u003e, with readings between 0% and 100%. It is \u003cstrong\u003eupdated on a daily basis\u003c/strong\u003e, on GMT close, and compared to the same data 5 days ago.\"]}]}},\"rates-charts\":{\"IndicatorsChart\":{\"assetSelector\":\"Asset\",\"searchPlaceholder\":\"Search assets...\"},\"SubHome\":{\"pageTitle\":\"Rates and Charts\",\"liveRates\":{\"sectionTitle\":\"Live Rates\",\"headline\":\"Your trading cockpit\",\"description\":\"This first glance through will train your eyes to know the prices of the major pairs, and give you a quick peek at essential trading information.\",\"cta\":\"Go to the Full Asset List\",\"error\":\"Live rates could not be loaded. Candlestick analysis further helps assess shifts in bullish or bearish momentum through formations such as doji, engulfing, or hammer patterns.\"}],\"westtexasintermediate\":[{\"question\":\"What is WTI?\",\"answer\":\"WTI refers to West Texas Intermediate crude Oil, specifically that produced in the United States (US). WTI Oil is traded on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) and is considered one of the main international benchmarks for Oil pricing. In financial markets, WTI US Oil refers to the price of one barrel in US Dollars (USD) and is presented as an exchange rate that fluctuates based on supply and demand dynamics. WTI US Oil is the second-most-popular commodity among investors after Gold, largely due to its high trading volume.\"},{\"question\":\"How can I forecast the WTI US Oil price?\",\"answer\":\"Market forecasting is very hard and models tend to fail to account for rapid changes and unexpected events, which can easily occur. Still, traders use multiple methods to analyze where the WTI US Oil price could be in the short, medium, and long term. Technical analysis focuses on chart patterns and mathematical indicators to anticipate future price movements. Fundamental or macroeconomic analysis looks at economic developments such as central bank policies, inflation, employment and growth data, which influence global demand for Oil. Sentiment analysis evaluates overall market risk appetite to determine whether Oil is likely to benefit from economic optimism or suffer during periods of uncertainty. Traders usually combine all these approaches.\"},{\"question\":\"What is the difference between WTI and Brent?\",\"answer\":\"WTI US Oil and Brent Oil are both crude Oil benchmarks but differ in origin, composition and transportation. WTI is landlocked US Oil, while Brent is extracted from the North Sea. WTI is lighter and sweeter, making it cheaper to refine into gasoline, whereas Brent is heavier and contains more sulfur. Brent is easier to ship globally and therefore tends to trade at a premium. Brent is also the primary international benchmark for Oil prices.\"},{\"question\":\"Which factors influence the WTI US Oil price?\",\"answer\":\"The price of WTI US Oil is mainly influenced by supply and demand dynamics. Decisions made by the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and its allies, collectively known as OPEC+, play a key role, as the group regularly sets production targets to influence prices. US Oil inventories and production levels are also important drivers. In addition, geopolitical tensions involving major Oil-producing regions can significantly impact WTI prices.\"},{\"question\":\"How can I trade WTI US Oil?\",\"answer\":\"Trading WTI US Oil involves buying or selling exposure to WTI crude against the US Dollar. Retail investors cannot exchange physical Oil, so most traders access WTI through brokers’ digital trading platforms. Trading commodities online typically offers low transaction costs, fast execution and the possibility to use leverage, depending on the trader’s risk tolerance.\"},{\"question\":\"How is technical analysis used in trading WTI US Oil?\",\"answer\":\"Technical analysis is widely used to forecast movements in the price of WTI US Oil. It involves analyzing historical price data to identify trends, chart patterns and key support and resistance levels, which can help determine entry and exit points. Traders also use indicators such as the Relative Strength Index (RSI), Momentum, Bollinger Bands and Moving Averages to confirm trend strength or identify overbought and oversold conditions. Candlestick analysis further helps assess shifts in bullish or bearish momentum through formations such as doji, engulfing or hammer patterns.\"}],\"dollarindexspot\":[{\"question\":\"What is the US Dollar Index (DXY)?\",\"answer\":\"The US Dollar Index (DXY) measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against a basket of six major currencies: the Euro (EUR), the Japanese Yen (JPY), the Pound Sterling (GBP), the Canadian Dollar (CAD), the Swiss Franc (CHF) and the Swedish Krona (SEK). The DXY is presented as an exchange rate that fluctuates based on supply and demand dynamics in the foreign exchange market. The relative strength of the United States (US) economy compared with the other economies in the basket, central bank policies, trade relations and political developments are among the key factors that influence the index. The DXY is one of the most popular assets among investors due to its high trading volumes and relatively low spreads.\"},{\"question\":\"Why is the US Dollar Index important?\",\"answer\":\"The US Dollar Index (DXY) is important because it is widely seen as a gauge of US economic strength and overall confidence in the US Dollar. The United States is the world’s largest economy, and the USD is the most widely used global currency. Many countries hold the USD as a reserve asset, and it is extensively used in international trade invoicing. As a result, movements in the DXY can have broad implications for global financial markets.\"},{\"question\":\"How can I forecast the US Dollar Index?\",\"answer\":\"Market forecasting is very hard and models often fail to account for rapid changes and unexpected events. Still, traders use several methods to analyze where the DXY could move in the short, medium and long term. Technical analysis involves studying price charts and mathematical indicators to anticipate future movements. Fundamental or macroeconomic analysis focuses on economic developments such as central bank policies, inflation, employment and growth data. Sentiment analysis assesses overall market risk perception to determine whether the US Dollar is likely to benefit from safe-haven flows or stronger risk appetite. Traders typically combine these approaches.\"},{\"question\":\"Which factors influence the US Dollar Index’s valuation?\",\"answer\":\"The valuation of the DXY is influenced by a wide range of economic and financial factors. The Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy decisions, driven by inflation trends, economic growth and labor market conditions, play a central role. In addition, fiscal policy, trade relations and political developments in the United States and in the economies of the basket currencies can affect demand and supply dynamics, influencing the index.\"},{\"question\":\"How is the DXY calculated?\",\"answer\":\"The DXY is calculated using a weighted geometric average of the exchange rates between the US Dollar and the six currencies in its basket. The Euro has the largest weight at 57.6%, followed by the Japanese Yen at 13.6%, the Pound Sterling at 11.9%, the Canadian Dollar at 9.1%, the Swedish Krona at 4.2% and the Swiss Franc at 3.6%.\"},{\"question\":\"How can I trade the US Dollar Index?\",\"answer\":\"Trading the US Dollar Index involves gaining exposure to the US Dollar against a basket of six major currencies. While it is possible to physically exchange US Dollars for other currencies, the DXY itself cannot be bought or sold physically. Instead, investors trade the index through brokers’ digital platforms, typically using derivatives. Trading the DXY online offers low transaction costs, fast execution times and, depending on the platform, the opportunity to use leverage, based on an investor’s risk tolerance.\"}]}},\"Header\":{\"title\":\"{assetName} Exchange rate\",\"tools\":\"Tools\",\"news\":\"News\",\"editorial\":\"Editorial\"},\"RateSingleAsset\":{\"updatedAt\":\"Updated at {date} GMT\"},\"RateSinglePercentChange\":{\"1D\":\"1 Day\",\"1W\":\"1 Week\",\"1M\":\"1 Month\",\"3M\":\"3 Months\",\"6M\":\"6 Months\",\"1Y\":\"1 Year\",\"YTD\":\"YTD\"},\"RateIntervals\":{\"1\":\"1 Min\",\"15\":\"15 Min\",\"60\":\"1 Hour\",\"240\":\"4 Hours\",\"1D\":\"1 Day\",\"1W\":\"1 Week\"},\"RatesAssetTable\":{\"assetsLinkLable\":\"Assets\",\"asset\":\"Asset\",\"last\":\"Last\",\"bid\":\"Bid\",\"ask\":\"Ask\",\"change\":\"CHG\",\"changePercent\":\"CHG%\",\"open\":\"Open\",\"high\":\"High\",\"low\":\"Low\"},\"RatesPage\":{\"title\":\"Forex Rates Table\",\"description\":\"Real-time interbank forex rates for more than 1,600 assets across different markets - Forex, Commodities and equities.\",\"FaqsSection\":{\"title\":\"Forex Rates FAQs\",\"faqs\":[{\"question\":\"What is the Forex rates table?\",\"answer\":\"Live rates for more than 1,600 assets across different markets (Forex, Commodities, Indices, Futures...). The index represents over 80% of the total market capitalization in the United Kingdom (UK). Stocks in the FTSE 100 are free-float weighted, ensuring that only the investable opportunity set is included in the index.\"]}],\"right\":[{\"title\":\"Japanese Equity Indices\",\"paragraphs\":[\"The \u003cstrong\u003eNikkei 225, commonly called the Nikkei\u003c/strong\u003e, is a stock market index for the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE). It has been calculated daily by the Nihon Keizai Shimbun (Nikkei) newspaper since 1970.\"]},{\"title\":\"Relationships between stocks and currencies\",\"paragraphs\":[\"Currencies are probably the most difficult asset class to fit into a consistent intermarket model. For instance, when investors purchase \u003cstrong\u003estocks\u003c/strong\u003e from a particular country, they must pay in the local currency, increasing the demand for that currency. Conversely, a strong currency can make bonds and stocks more attractive to foreign investors.\",\"However, the correlation between stocks and currencies is not always clear. There are often response lags between the reactions of Forex and equities markets, leaving investors holding foreign equities \u003cstrong\u003eexposed to exchange rate ﬂuctuations\u003c/strong\u003e.\",\"This correlation is also fragile among international equity markets. The so-called \u003cstrong\u003eglobal divergences\u003c/strong\u003e occur when the stock market in one country starts performing better than the stock market in another country. Nevertheless, one of the arguably most closely watched market drivers is Fedspeak – a form of forward guidance that contains official and alternative communications by the Federal Reserve (Fed) officials.\",\"decipheringP2\":\"In the recently updated FAQ section of its official website, the Fed explains:\",\"decipheringFedQuote\":\"Forward guidance is a tool that central banks use to tell the public about the likely future course of monetary policy. The Fed doesn't take asset prices into consideration when setting its monetary policy. That, however, doesn't change the fact that monetary policy decisions and comments on the outlook have a significant impact on financial markets.\",\"figureFedFundsAlt\":\"Fed funds rate (2020-2025)\",\"figureFedFundsCaption\":\"Fed funds rate (2020-2025)\",\"powellP1\":\"For instance, the Fed announced that it left the interest rate unchanged at the range of 5.25%-5.5% at the July 2024 policy meeting. These comments revived optimism about the US central bank shifting into monetary easing, triggering a US Dollar (USD) selloff and boosting US equity indexes.\",\"speechTrackerP1\":\"Interpreting comments from Fed policymakers and reading between the lines in official communications is not an easy task, especially for beginner traders. This allows us to provide traders with real-time notifications on our Economic Calendar on how each Fedspeak could influence the USD's valuation.\",\"figureEcocalAlt\":\"Speech Tracker scores on FXStreet Economic Calendar\",\"figureEcocalCaption\":\"Speech Tracker scores on FXStreet Economic Calendar\",\"introducingTitle\":\"Introducing FXStreet Fed Sentiment Index\",\"introducingP1\":\"The next step in our quest to provide the best tool to help traders assess the effect of the Fed's language on financial markets was to use Speech Tracker scores to calculate an aggregate index that paints a clear picture of how the sentiment changes over time: FXStreet Fed Sentiment Index.\",\"introducingP2\":\"FXStreet Fed Sentiment Index presents the Fed's tone as a single value, taking into consideration comments from all voting and non-voting members of the FOMC in TV appearances, conferences, interviews, as well as the Fed's official written communications and more.\",\"introducingP3\":\"A value of 100 represents a neutral tone. An increasing value above 100 points to a hawkish tilt in the Fed's language, while a decreasing value below 100 suggests a dovish change in sentiment. Learn about FED's impact on currencies: News \u0026 Analysis to help you get the most profit out of monetary policy decisions.\",\"keywords\":\"fed, forex, us, minutes, fomc, federal reserve\",\"pageTitle\":\"FOMC Interest rate decision (Fed) | News \u0026 Analysis\",\"socialImageUrl\":\"https://editorial.azureedge.net/images/Macroeconomics/CentralBanks/FED/federal-reserve-building-gm490074826-75019399_XtraSmall.jpg\"},\"faqs\":[{\"question\":\"What's important about the Federal Reserve's monetary policy meeting?\",\"answer\":\"With a pre-set regularity, a nation's central bank holds a monetary policy meeting where board members take different measures, the most relevant one setting the range of the federal funds rate, which greatly influences the interest rate charge on loans and advances to commercial banks. In the US, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) of the Federal Reserve (Fed) meets at intervals of five to eight weeks to announce their latest decisions. An interest-rate hike increases borrowing costs throughout the economy. This results in a stronger US Dollar (USD) as it makes the US a more attractive place for international investors. A rate cut, on the other hand, tends to weaken the USD. If rates remain unchanged, the attention, main news and analysis turn to the tone of the monetary policy statement and the press conference from the Fed's Chair. Markets analyze whether the tone is hawkish or dovish over future developments of inflation.\"},{\"question\":\"What is the Fed?\",\"answer\":\"The Federal Reserve (Fed) is the central bank of the United States (US) and it has two main targets: to maintain the unemployment rate at its lowest possible levels and to keep inflation around 2%. The Federal Reserve System's structure is composed of the presidentially appointed Board of Governors and the partially appointed Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). The FOMC organizes eight scheduled meetings in a year to review economic and financial conditions. It also determines the appropriate stance of monetary policy and assesses the risks to its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth. The FOMC Minutes, which are released by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve weeks after the latest meeting, are a guide to the future US interest-rate policy. Fed official website, on X and Facebook.\"},{\"question\":\"How to trade the event?\",\"answer\":\"\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003eDo not rely on the Fed to determine the direction of the dollar in the coming months.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThe dollar tends to follow its predominant trend when the Fed starts to hike rates.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eThere is no direct link between the Fed hiking rates and the usd falling. When a weak usd has coincided with a Fed hiking cycle, it has been falling for some time.\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli\u003eDue to this, we may see a muted reaction to a potential Fed rate hike.\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\"},{\"question\":\"Who is FOMC's chairman?\",\"answer\":\"Kevin Warsh took office as chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve in May 2026, for a four-year term ending in 2030. His term as a member of the Board of Governors will expire in May 2040. Warsh, born in Albany (New York) on April 13, 1970, is an American financier and attorney who already served as a member of the Fed Board of Governors from 2006 to 2011 and was significantly involved in the central bank's response to the financial crisis. Before that, he served as a special assistant to the president for economic policy and the executive secretary of the National Economic Council under President George W. Bush.\"}]},\"ecb\":{\"seo\":{\"title\":\"ECB Preview (European Central Bank)\",\"description\":\"What to expect From ECB? Learn about European Central Bank's decisions and its impact on currencies: Advice to help you get the most profit out of monetary policy decisions.\",\"keywords\":\"ecb, european central bank, ecb preview, european central bank rate decision\",\"pageTitle\":\"ECB (European Central Bank)\",\"socialImageUrl\":\"https://editorial.azureedge.net/images/Macroeconomics/CentralBanks/ECB/ecb-european-central-bank-frankfurt-germany-60028418_XtraSmall.jpg\"},\"faqs\":[{\"question\":\"What is the ECB?\",\"answer\":\"The European Central Bank (ECB) is the central bank empowered to manage monetary policy for the Eurozone. With its beginnings in Germany in 1998, the ECB's mandate is to maintain price stability in the Eurozone, so that the Euro's (EUR) purchasing power is not eroded by inflation. As an entity independent of individual European Union countries and institutions, the ECB targets a year-on-year increase in consumer prices of 2% over the medium term. Another of its tasks is controlling the money supply. This involves, for instance, setting interest rates throughout the Eurozone. The European Central Bank's work is organized via the following decision-making bodies: the Executive Board, the Governing Council and the General Council. Christine Lagarde has been the President of the ECB since November 1, 2019. Her speeches, statements and comments are an important source of volatility, especially for the Euro and the currencies traded against the European currency.\"},{\"question\":\"Who is ECB's President?\",\"answer\":\"Christine Lagarde was born in 1956 in Paris, France. Lagarde, who graduated from Paris West University Nanterre La DÃ©fense, became President of the European Central Bank (ECB) on November 1, 2019. Prior to that, she served as Chairman and Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) between 2011 and 2019. Lagarde previously held various senior ministerial posts in the Government of France: she was Minister of the Economy, Finance and Industry (2007-2011), Minister of Agriculture and Fishing (2007) and Minister of Commerce (2005-2007).\"},{\"question\":\"How to trade the ECB interest-rate decision\",\"answer\":\"$27\"},{\"question\":\"Hike, cut or keep interest rates unchanged\",\"answer\":\"The European Central Bank's (ECB) decision on interest rates always has an effect on the Euro (EUR). When interest rates increase, the European Central Bank is selling government securities to large financial firms. In turn, the financial organizations are paying in euros for these securities. This effectively decreases the amount of currency circulating in the economy. A decreasing supply leads to higher demand and therefore causes the value of the Euro to appreciate. When the interest rates decrease, the European Central Bank floods the market with euros. This is done by purchasing government securities from financial organizations. In return for the securities, these banks and financial deals are paid in euros, therefore increasing the supply of euros in the economy. As supply increases, the value of the Euro depreciates.\"},{\"question\":\"Some concepts you need to know\",\"answer\":\"In practical terms, QE means that central banks create money out of nothing to buy securities, such as government bonds. This new money swells the size of bank reserves by the quantity of assets purchased and that's why this programme is called Quantitative Easings. The money supply is intended to flood financial institutions with capital in an effort to stimulate lending and increase liquidity. Much of the governments' debt is held by banks in the Eurozone and the ECB wants them to give more credits. If the European Central Bank buys government bonds, their prices rise and profitability drop even more. This is a liquidity-providing operation that weakens the value of the euro. This depreciation makes European exports cheaper and competitive, and ultimately, helps in recovering. In addition, as a result of the stimulus to internal and external consumption, the ECB combats the risk of deflation, a widespread and prolonged drop in prices, as well as the high unemployment.\"}]},\"boe\":{\"seo\":{\"title\":\"Bank of England (BoE) - Forex News \u0026 Articles\",\"description\":\"What to expect from the Bank of England? The Bank of England is responsible for maintaining the UK's economic stability.
